image_description: A side-profile view of a hammerhead shark swimming in deep blue water, facing left. The image captures the anterior half of the shark, prominently displaying the cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head), gill slits, pectoral fin, and first dorsal fin. The caudal fin is not visible within the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The iconic T-shaped head structure is clearly visible and dominates the left side of the composition.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark eye structures are discernible at the outermost edges of the hammer head, consistent with species anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Resolution and lighting prevent distinct visualization of nares; they blend into the ventral surface texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front edge appears relatively straight with a subtle central notch, suggesting Scalloped Hammerhead morphology rather than the straight edge of a Great Hammerhead.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The torso tapers smoothly and appears thin from this side angle, indicating correct lateral compression.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Standard countershading is evident: darker grey dorsally transitioning to a lighter/white underbelly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Image resolution is insufficient to resolve individual dermal denticles; skin appears artificially smooth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The prominent dorsal fin is visible, tall, and exhibits the characteristic sickle curve.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible pectoral fin is large, triangular, and positioned correctly behind the gills.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail section is completely cropped out of the right-side frame boundary.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Gill slits appear somewhat fused or 'melted' into the body surface rather than having distinct, sharp separations. The transition between the jaw and cheek lacks crisp anatomical definition.
Eyes lack clear pupil/iris distinction and appear as smudged dark spots, common in AI generations struggling with small high-contrast details.
